title: compact-reading-log-llm-inference-notes-marcus-flynn-2026-12
content:
Quick personal digest: a short, punchy log of a few papers/blogs I skimmed today and the experiments I want to try. Keep this tight — I’ll expand into separate notes if anything needs deep dives.

1) Paper: "Efficient Attention Improvements" (arXiv gist + blog) — tl;dr:
- Main idea: small kernel-level changes + fused CUDA kernels give ~1.2–1.8x speedups for medium sequence lengths (1k-8k) without changing model weights.
- My hot take: most wins are for self-attention dense paths; KV-cache heavy workloads still bottleneck on memory bandwidth and KV scatter/gather.
- Possible Redwood experiment: benchmark their fused kernel vs our runtime on a 16k-config request pattern (50% short, 30% mid, 20% long). Measure p99 latency and gpu_util per model shard.
- Quick TODO: add micro-benchmark harness under /bench/kv-cache-sim that simulates 500 concurrent chat sessions with variable history lengths.

2) Blog: "Per-token Quantization And When It Breaks" — notes:
- Claim: aggressive per-token quantization (8-bit per token packing) can break distributional properties on rare token generation, causing hallucinations for low-frequency prompts.
- Observation: degradation shows up in top-k tail probability shift, not always BLEU/ROUGE. Need targeted metrics (log-prob slope on tail).
- Redwood implication: when recommending quant profiles in Optimize, surface a "tail-robustness" metric and example failing prompts.
- Experiment: take our 13B float->qat8 profile and run 1000 targeted prompts that stress punctuation/rare-entity completions. Track KL-divergence of token distribution compared to fp16 baseline.

3) Paper: "Routing Cost in Mixture-of-Experts for Retrieval-Augmented Generation" — quick notes:
- Focus: latency variance from expert lookups and routing overhead outweighs model compute for small requests.
- Engineering note: dynamic routing adds branching that destroys throughput on GPU pipelines; batching helps but increases tail latency.
- Idea: consider a hybrid policy inside Redwood: light-weight ensemble (2 experts) with synchronous fallback rather than wide sparse MoE. Simpler for Dedicated customers with tight p99 SLAs.
- Experiment: simulate 3 routing policies on our workload trace (sticky-user sessions): (a) wide MoE, (b) 2-expert sync, (c) single-expert + async second-call. Measure cost/sec, effective throughput, and p99.

4) Short reading: "Prefix and Hierarchical KV caching" (conference slides + talk notes)
- Key point: hierarchical cache with short-prefix hot-slotting reduces repeated recomputation for assistants that frequently re-open context (e.g., agent recall).
- Implementation thought: cheap bloom-filter index for prefixes to avoid KV lookups for cold sessions. Might save mem-bandwidth in Dedicated.
- Quick hack: prototype an LRU-tiered KV store in the runtime that promotes entries based on hit-rate over a sliding window (30m).

Common experiments / cross-cutting concerns:
- Metric primitives to add for all experiments: per-token bandwidth (GB/s), GPU memcpy time breakdown, number of KV cache misses, and top-token distribution KL vs baseline. We should capture these at token granularity for a sample of sessions, not all (sample 1%).
- Add an "Eval probe set" of 200 targeted prompts that are sensitive to quantization and cache invalidation (examples below). This becomes the canonical smoke test for Optimize recommendations.

Concrete next steps (short sprint):
- [ ] Create bench harness: sources/bench/kv-cache-sim (owner: me) — due 2026-12-10
- [ ] Put together eval probe set (200 prompts) and store in repo redwood/evals/probes/quant-kv-2026
- [ ] Run fused-kernel vs runtime baseline on 4 models: 7B, 13B, 33B, 70B (sample traces) — capture p50/p95/p99 and token bandwidth
- [ ] Prototype LRU-tiered KV store in a feature-flagged branch (runtime/kvcache/tiered) — spike estimate: 3 days

Notes-to-self:
- When running quant experiments, lock RNG seeds and deterministic sampling for comparison (top-k deterministic).
- Keep a log of example failure generations to attach to Optimize UI test cases.
- Coordinate with Owen on adding the new metrics to observability (traces + token traces): pinged him in the linked ticket.

Example failing prompts (seed list for probe set) — short, adversarial style:
- "Generate a plausible scientific paper title mentioning a rare chemical: qv-348z"
- "Summarize this long list of obscure wiki dates into a timeline (dates only)"
- "Complete the citation: Smith et al., 2012, on preconditioners for —"

Questions for team sync:
- How aggressive do we want Optimize to be in recommending quant profiles vs highlighting uncertainty? (safety-first?)
- For Dedicated customers: are there capacity/contract restrictions that prevent us from shipping experimental kernel changes on their clusters? (ops and legal check)

References / links I found during reading:
- Efficient attention kernels (summary blog): https://example-blog.org/fast-attn-kernels
- Per-token quant pitfalls (thread): https://ml-forum.org/thread/quant-per-token-issues
- MoE routing costs (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01645

End note: keep this as a living compact log. If an item becomes heavier, split into a proper doc under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml.
